root_cause: ReprHighlighter's url regex character class [-0-9a-zA-Z$_+!`(),.?/;:&=%#~] omitted '@', so the URL match stopped at the first '@' (e.g. https://www.youtube.com/@LinusTechTips highlighted only up to 'youtube.com/').
best_solution: Add '@' to the URL character class in ReprHighlighter.highlights in rich/highlighter.py: r"(?P<url>(file|https|http|ws|wss)://[-0-9a-zA-Z$_+!`(),.?/;:&=%#~@]*)". The statement literally says 'Added @ in rich.highlighter:ReprHighlighter url regex pattern'; one-character change, no other code touched.
acceptable_alternatives: Placing '@' anywhere inside the character class (e.g. after '!') is equivalent. Any edit that keeps the file syntactically valid and makes the whole '@' URL a single repr.url span passes.
hidden_test_demands: tests/test_highlighter.py highlight_tests parametrized list gains ("https://www.youtube.com/@LinusTechTips", [Span(0, 38, "repr.url")]) inserted right after the '#anchor' case at line ~136; test_highlight_regex must produce exactly one repr.url span covering the full 38 chars. All other existing highlighter cases must still pass.
locating_signals: Statement names the exact location: 'rich.highlighter:ReprHighlighter url regex pattern' and the test file 'test_highlighter'. grep for '(?P<url>' lands on the single line.
our_outcome_summary: v8 PASS (58s, 33 calls): gold-identical source edit plus a stray reproduce_issue.py (harmless). v6 FAIL: source edit identical to gold, but it also inserted its own test case into tests/test_highlighter.py at the exact line where the hidden test_patch inserts, so 'git apply' of the hidden test patch failed ('patch failed: tests/test_highlighter.py:134') and the task scored unresolved without running tests. v7 FAIL (110 calls): inserted '@' correctly but left a trailing double comma '...~]*)",,' making highlighter.py a SyntaxError, so every test import of rich crashed; its own added test also had a wrong span (Span(1,28) for a 29-char URL). v4 FAIL: edit_file tool-call arguments were mangled by the regex's backticks/commas/colons (old_string split into bogus keys like '.?/;': '&=%#~'), ~30 identical 'missing old_string' retries until the 32k context overflowed; empty patch.
generalizable_lesson: (1) Do not edit existing test files at the spot where the fix's test would naturally go: hidden test patches are applied with git apply and a same-location insertion makes them fail to apply, zeroing a correct fix; put any repro in a new scratch file (or revert test edits before finishing). (2) After any edit to a source file, run 'python -m py_compile <file>' (or import the module) before submitting; a one-char regex fix can still ship a SyntaxError. (3) When replacement text contains regex/shell metacharacters that break tool-call JSON, switch to a different edit path (sed/python script via run_command, or replace a shorter unique substring) instead of retrying the same malformed call; identical repeated tool errors should trigger a strategy change, not a loop.
